## Scope

This is a maintainer-facing historical design record. It originated with an
audit of the early public 0.1.0 codebase and was updated on 2026-08-20 after the
resource-management, ESEM-quality, accounting, and telemetry work described
below. It is **not** the source of truth for the current package API or current
calculation defaults; use the function documentation and the methodological-
foundations vignette for those. The audit did not establish runtime speedups or
compare optimizer families. Everything labeled deferred, planned, a design
target, a test candidate, or experimental remains a roadmap item rather than a
claim about current package behavior.

SEMANTICA supports response-free item-pool development and structural
screening. Its embedding-derived diagnostics can help identify redundancy,
content gaps, and candidate structures before responses are collected. They do
not establish construct validity. A selected form remains a candidate for a
locked analysis using participant response data.

## Current Search Model

`ACO_with_ESEM()` currently performs a factor-stratified binary subset search.
Item-to-factor membership comes from metadata and is neither inferred nor
reassigned. For factor-specific eligible sets and requested counts, the nominal
space before duplicate-cluster proposal guarding has the following
fixed-cardinality representation:

```text
I = disjoint union over f of I_f
x_i in {0,1}
sum_{i in I_f} x_i = k_f for every factor f
x_i = 0 for items outside the eligible set E_f
|X| = product_f choose(|E_f|, k_f)
```

Construction enforces the requested count for each factor. Its duplicate-aware
guard can further restrict proposals while alternatives remain and can fall
back when avoidance is infeasible. Most other qualities, including redundancy, facet
coverage, proxy fit, loading quality, HTMT, and the current psychometric guards,
are scores, multipliers, diagnostics, or soft penalties rather than one strict
admissibility rule. The default `pfa_mode = "diagnostic"` reports PFA output but
gives it zero weight in the search objective. `model_type` is an unused
compatibility placeholder in this release.

When enabled during search, ESEM fits a correlation structure derived from item
embeddings. Without participant responses, ESEM, PFA, and DFI are sample-free
proxy diagnostics. They can screen candidate forms, but they cannot demonstrate
reliability, invariance, response processes, or construct validity. Response
data supplied through validation paths are used after selection and do not
retroactively convert the search proxy into validation evidence.

The current implementation also has optimizer boundaries worth making explicit.
The public worker default remains two, but there is no artificial two-worker
ceiling. `semantica_resource_plan()` resolves serial, explicit, or `"auto"`
worker requests against the CPU allocation visible to R and an optional
`max.cores`; `reserve.cores` applies to automatic selection. Parallel execution
uses one SEMANTICA-owned PSOCK pool with single-threaded worker BLAS settings to
reduce nested oversubscription.

ESEM scoring now begins with a common mathematical admissibility assessment.
It checks convergence, a post-fit check when the installed `lavaan` version
exposes one, finite standardized matrices and estimates, residual variances,
and the validity and positive definiteness of the latent covariance matrix.
Unavailable post-fit checking is reported rather than treated as automatic
failure. Admissible solutions are then aligned to the intended factor axes by a
deterministic one-to-one loading match and intended-item sign anchors; the same
permutation and sign transformation is applied to the loading and latent
covariance matrices. Non-admissible or unalignable fits do not receive a finite
search-time ESEM score. These checks are mathematical quality gates, not
substantive loading cutoffs or evidence of construct validity.

The canonical `elite_multicriteria_rerank` option applies a scalar final rerank or bonus; the deprecated `elite_pareto_rerank` name is retained only as a compatibility alias. It
does not maintain a Pareto-dominance archive and is not MOACO.

SEMANTICA 0.2.10 also records `objective_context`. This does not change the
objective calculation. It records whether the final utility came from ESEM-guided
reranking, semantic/PFA guidance, or an explicit fallback. The numeric objective
is an optimizer utility under that regime, not a universal between-run measure of
scale quality. This distinction is especially important after fallback because
the active evidence components differ.

`run_multi_seed_semantica()` therefore also returns `objective_comparability`.
Objective dispersion is still preserved for reproducibility, but when successful
seeds span different evidence regimes it is explicitly marked as unsuitable for
interpretation on one common quality scale. Item-set frequencies and Jaccard
stability remain interpretable descriptive summaries regardless of that regime
mismatch.

## Resource Accounting

The audit uses the following source-level cost decomposition:

```text
T_total =
  T_pre/DFI + T_construction + N_unique,cheap * T_cheap
  + N_unique,ESEM * T_ESEM + T_parallel/serialization + T_final
```

This decomposition identifies distinct evaluation events rather than treating a
request, duplicate, cache hit, candidate job, low-level solver attempt, and DFI
simulation as interchangeable. SEMANTICA now has an incremental broker for
search-time ESEM checkpoints. It constructs canonical subset keys, coalesces
duplicate requests within a batch, reuses central-cache outcomes, reserves the
budget before dispatch, and records requests, unique candidates, cache hits,
coalesced requests, candidate jobs started, converged and admissible results,
failed results, and observed solver attempts.

Accordingly, `max_esem_fits` now limits **unique search-time ESEM candidate jobs
admitted to execution**. Cache hits and coalesced duplicate requests do not
consume that budget. The unit is a candidate job, not a low-level solver start:
one admitted candidate can still invoke a fallback solver attempt. Archive
reranking fits, final or sensitivity fits, response-validation fits, and DFI
simulation jobs are reported separately and remain outside this search cap.
`max.iter` remains patience for non-improvement or stagnation, while
`max_total_iter` is the optional total-iteration ceiling.

Returned `evaluation_telemetry` exposes the search counters plus separate
archive, final, and DFI counts. `$performance` records resolved resources,
CPU/GPU compute decisions where applicable, stage timings, evaluation counts,
candidate evaluations, and iterations; `$reproducibility` records the master
seed, task seeds, RNG state/kind, effective workers, optimizer settings, and
relevant versions. DFI counts cover SEMANTICA simulation stages that expose
telemetry; third-party dynamic or DDD-FI internals may not expose every fit
start. Thus this is a useful accounting foundation, not yet a generalized
cross-stage evaluation service with deadlines, timeouts, a uniform retry
policy, or one shared cache for every evaluator.

Full-pool cosine construction is also instrumented. CPU/double precision is the
safe default, and `compute_device = "auto"` currently resolves to CPU. Users may
explicitly request an available R `torch` CUDA device, or MPS with explicitly
requested single precision, with an explicit error-or-CPU fallback policy and
an optional memory limit. This optional path does not accelerate ACO, `lavaan`,
DFI, or batched semantic scoring, and no benchmark-based CPU/GPU crossover has
been established.

## Priority Roadmap

The priority vocabulary is fixed: **P0: blocks trustworthy optimization or
interpretation. P1: best-supported performance work after P0. P2:
analysis/scaling work after P0/P1. P3: exploratory research work.**

| Priority | Change | Current status | Remaining release or evidence gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Canonical evaluation broker, central deduplication/cache filtering, true unique-fit accounting, separate DFI ledger, finite resource caps, and telemetry. | Search-time ESEM brokering and stage-aware counters are implemented; a generalized cross-stage broker is deferred. | Extend common keys, cache/retry policy, deadlines, and exact start accounting to every evaluator; verify serial/parallel equivalence and all cap/failure paths. |
| P0 | Centralized ESEM convergence/propriety/admissibility predicate and rotated factor-column/sign alignment before scoring. | Implemented as the current correctness gate, with returned reasons and alignment diagnostics. | Retain improper, nonfinite, permuted, sign-flipped, and large-factor fixtures as release regressions; keep rejected fits out of guided scoring. |
| P0 | Explicit resources and randomness: total-iteration/patience/fit/deadline limits, deterministic streams, returned RNG/config metadata, and memory-aware worker handling. | Allocation-aware PSOCK planning, iteration/search-fit limits, seed-derived task streams, and returned resource/reproducibility telemetry are implemented. | Add a global deadline and evidence-based memory-derived worker sizing; demonstrate candidate/accounting equivalence across scheduling orders and worker counts. |
| P1 | Configured EAS, canonical RAS, subset-MMAS, and ACS comparison on one common evaluator/scaffold; no predeclared winner. | Planned comparative experiment. | Held-out, matched-budget results justify any default change against corrected legacy and non-ACO baselines. |
| P1 | Partial-subset marginal heuristic for target-band loss, redundancy, between-factor burden, facet/content quotas, and constraint slack. | Experimental design target. | Delta calculations match full recomputation and improve held-out anytime results after construction cost is counted. |
| P1 | Audited multi-fidelity promotion using cheap elite, diverse, and uniform-random audit strata. | Experimental design target. | Small exact problems establish gate recall; larger audits retain known nonzero random inclusion probabilities. |
| P1 | Bounded feasible within-factor 1-swap local search and meaningful smoothing/restart. | Planned test candidate. | Net gain is shown at the same total unique-fit budget without unacceptable diversity or runtime loss. |
| P2 | Stability outputs and nondominated audit archive; do not label current scalar rerank as Pareto. | Semantic pair-perturbation stability is returned (with the legacy split-half alias); a nondominated archive is deferred. | Known-front tests pass and validation remains isolated from archive-based selection. |
| P3 | Learned surrogates, full MOACO, asynchronous exchange, and broader GPU work only after the exact-data pipeline and held-out benchmarks justify them. | Explicit optional R `torch` full-pool cosine exists; automatic GPU choice, GPU ESEM/DFI, and the other research extensions are deferred. | Each backend beats simpler tuned alternatives at equal end-to-end held-out cost and retains exact finalist confirmation. |

The former nonnegotiable prerequisite--**one ESEM mathematical-admissibility
rule plus factor-axis alignment**--is now implemented and should remain a
release regression gate. It is a correctness feature, not performance evidence,
and it does not by itself support claims about optimizer-family superiority.

## Mathematical Design Targets

The following equations describe future designs and test candidates; they are
not current SEMANTICA features. A future one-trail inclusion constructor can use
the partial-subset rule

```text
p(i | C_t) =
  tau_i^alpha * eta_i(x_1:t-1)^beta
  / sum_{j in C_t} tau_j^alpha * eta_j(x_1:t-1)^beta
```

over additions that can still produce a feasible completion. The heuristic must
remain positive and normalized within the current choice set. One experimental
marginal form is

```text
log eta_i =
  -lambda_1 * Delta L_target
  -lambda_2 * Delta R_max
  -lambda_3 * Delta B_between
  +lambda_4 * Delta C_facet
  +lambda_5 * S_slack
```

The coefficients require configuration and ablation; the literature does not
establish their values for SEMANTICA. Candidate lists must retain an exploration
floor so that a strong heuristic does not silently recreate the present
irreversible gate.

Canonical RAS can be tested with the subset update

```text
tau_i <- (1 - rho) * tau_i +
  {sum_{r=1}^{w-1} (w-r) * 1[i in x_it^(r)]
   + w * 1[i in x_gb]} / Z
```

where the best `w - 1` iteration subsets receive decreasing weight and the
global best receives its separate weight `w`. A subset-MMAS candidate is

```text
tau_i <- clip_{[tau_min,f, tau_max,f]}(
  (1 - rho) * tau_i + Delta * 1[i in x*]
)
```

Each displayed pheromone equation is the complete update, including exactly one
evaporation operation. It must not be described or implemented as an additional
deposit following a separate evaporation step. Deposit scales and trail bounds
must be calibrated for without-replacement subset selection rather than copied
unchanged from routing problems. Only comparably evaluated, admissible exact
solutions should drive exact-objective pheromone updates.

## Benchmark and Release Gates

The benchmark has three complementary layers. **Exact small subset problems**
must be enumerable, including duplicate, quota, imbalanced-pool, prefilter, and
failure fixtures; they establish optima, gate recall, sampling probabilities,
and algorithm invariants. **Controlled synthetic psychometric/proxy problems**
must vary factor structure, loadings, cross-loadings, correlations, wording,
sample size, response type, misspecification, content scarcity, and fit failure.
Their semantic generator must not simply copy the psychometric population
correlation. **Empirical pools with response data** must include at least three
distinct pool structures and separate development, locked inner-selection, and
untouched outer or external validation data.

Required baselines are random feasible sampling, greedy construction plus
swaps, simulated annealing, tabu search, a fixed-cardinality genetic algorithm,
corrected legacy SEMANTICA, EAS, canonical RAS, subset-MMAS, ACS, and a
preregistered memetic extension of the development-set ACO winner. Every method
must use the same evaluator, candidate pool, constraints, frozen calibration and
objective, machine allocation, and final-refit rules. Objective
weights must not be tuned in the same race as optimizer settings.

Primary budgets are 50, 100, 250, 500, and, where feasible, 1000 unique
search-time fast-ESEM candidate jobs, using the implemented `max_esem_fits`
definition. Observed fallback solver attempts, DFI simulations, archive and
final fits, and end-to-end wall time must also be reported separately. All runs,
timeouts, failed or inadmissible fits, cache/coalescing behavior, and anytime
traces belong in the comparison; unused budget does not count as additional
solution quality.

The top three remaining interventions to test are:

1. Extend the incremental ESEM broker into a generalized, cross-stage evaluator
   with explicit timeout and retry semantics.
2. Configured bounded update-family comparison with real stagnation recovery.
3. Constraint-preserving, budget-capped elite swaps.

A component should become a default only after it improves a preregistered
anytime endpoint on held-out inner-selection instances by a meaningful margin,
meets locked response-validation noninferiority criteria, avoids a material rise
in improper or failed fits, and does not impose a harmful slowdown. The chosen
method and form must then be locked before the untouched outer test.

## What Not To Claim Yet

- Do not claim universal ACO superiority or a predetermined winner among EAS,
  canonical RAS, MMAS, and ACS.
- Do not describe the incremental search-time broker as a complete generalized
  evaluation service, or interpret `max_esem_fits` as an end-to-end cap. It
  limits unique search-time ESEM candidate jobs, not fallback solver attempts,
  archive/final refits, or DFI work.
- Do not call the current scalar `elite_multicriteria_rerank` behavior Pareto
  optimization, a nondominated archive, or MOACO.
- Do not claim semantic similarity or proxy ESEM/PFA validates constructs. A
  stable archive or attractive proxy fit is not respondent-data validation or
  proof of a global optimum.
- Do not claim automatic GPU selection, benchmarked GPU speedups, or GPU-backed
  ACO, `lavaan`, DFI, or batched semantic scoring. The current optional GPU path
  is an explicitly selected R `torch` implementation for full-pool cosine
  construction (plus separately configured local-model inference).
- Learned surrogates, full MOACO, adaptive controllers, asynchronous exchange,
  and broader GPU work remain P3 opportunities until the exact-data pipeline
  and held-out evidence justify their additional complexity.
